Hi! I was actually wondering if is it better for 'health' of my PC to keep it running all day long (and night), or if it is actually better turning it off after each session? I hope this is not an offtopic or something :D

The only moving parts in a computer these days are the fans and if you have any non-SS drives. So long as your machine is well ventilated. Leaving it running 24/7 is no problem. Unless you hate wasting electricity.

Fans need to be re-oiled once every year or two to keep form wearing out and spinning hard drives can die from being worn out. But, turning them on and off again is actually worse for them than just leaving them on all the time. So, there's really nothing to worry about.
Thank you. I was keeping my PC running for about ~week always and then I started to wonder if I shouldn't finally shut it down for a night to keep it resting. You helped me a lot! :)

Fans need to be re-oiled once every year or two to keep form wearing out and spinning hard drives can die from being worn out.

What was the last part about? You want to oil your hard drive? Sorry but the whole oiling fans is far too old. They last a couple years or longer. Generally the motors start to give out before oiling them actually does any good to keep them going.

It’s fine to leave your PC on. Physically there is negligible wear and tear if your PC is on but idle; some fans are running but those are rated to outlast the electronic parts. Electronically most modern PCs and operating systems will take care of themselves (run some diagnostics while idle, then go to sleep after a while).

My computers go months at a time without shutting down, and only reboot due to system updates.
Thank you. Exactly the answer I wanted to hear, much appreciate it :)

So long as your fans are working properly to keep your 'engine' cool, it's fine to leave it on. In fact, a lot of people tend to leave their computers 'up' for weeks, even months. Some servers have uptimes spanning years, so as long as there isn't a preexisting issue and your computer isn't in a situation where it might overheat (poor ventilation, up against a curtain, etc.) you should be fine.

Personally, I leave mine on for about a week. I like to run all my scans, updates and 'cleanses' on Sunday nights, at which point it shuts down and I start fresh Monday morning. It's like your shorts; it's up to ya!
